basics.name: Isaac Herman
basics.summary: Data analyst with 5 years of experience in measurement research and analytics, now pursuing a master's in data science.

work.name: Pinterest
highlights: Built privacy safe tool to estimate causal impact of ads without user-level data utilizing a Time-Based Regression and Geo Experiment framework, generated $XM incremental spend from advertisers

Engineered data pipeline to store metrics from advertising experiments, saving 50 hours of review time weekly and replacing over 10,000 separate reports with the company’s first central database of experimental results

Built dashboards to automate meta-analysis of advertising experiments using Inverse Variance Weighting methodology, enabled self-serve analysis and delivery of updated trends on a daily basis (instead of quarterly)

Identified 300 advertisers at highest risk of signal loss from cookie deprecation and built dashboard to track adoption of cookieless products, ensuring continued visibility into $XXB of conversion value
Developed internal tool for retail accounts to perform customer segmentation and calculate LTV along with XGBoost classification model to identify high-value customers for targeting purposes

work.name: SeatGeek
highlights: Implemented linear regression model to predict team ticketing revenue based on win-loss and market data
Built internal tool to scrape competitor pricing with Python

work.name: LionBird Ventures
highlights: Prepared market research reports and generated market penetration strategies for portfolio companies
Sourced deals at demo days and tech conferences, conducting due diligence to evaluate risk and value

work.name: TAMID Group Chapter at Tufts University
highlights: Founded Tufts chapter of non-profit organization that provides students with business education, pro-bono consulting opportunities, and summer fellowships
Oversaw educational curriculum and member recruitment (100+ students)
Coordinated projects for data science, consulting, and equity research teams
Organized several guest speaking events and raised over $10,000 in chapter funding
